title: The SecurityContextDeny admission plugin no longer exists — an API server that enables it will not start

detection.reason: the admission plugin list lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

quote: The deprecated `SecurityContextDeny` admission plugin, which has been deprecated since `v1.27`, has been removed.
remediation: Remove `SecurityContextDeny` from `--enable-admission-plugins` on every kube-apiserver before rolling to 1.30; an unknown plugin name is a startup error. Pod Security Admission (built in since 1.25, `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce` on the namespace) is the replacement.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?' | grep -- --enable-admission-plugins  # a value naming SecurityContextDeny stops kube-apiserver at 1.30

title: kubectl apply --prune-whitelist is gone — pipelines that pass it fail on a 1.30 kubectl

detection.reason: kubectl invocations live in CI and operator scripts, not in a cluster object

quote: kubectl: Removed the deprecated flag `prune-whitelist` for apply. Please use the flag `prune-allowlist` instead.
remediation: Replace `--prune-whitelist` with `--prune-allowlist` in CI jobs and scripts that run `kubectl apply --prune`; a 1.30 kubectl rejects the old flag as unknown. This is a client change: the cluster is unaffected, and an older kubectl keeps working within the supported skew.
verifyCommand: grep -rn -- '--prune-whitelist' . 2>/dev/null | head  # run in the repo that holds your deploy scripts; every hit breaks on a 1.30 kubectl

title: Out-of-tree PostFilter plugins must treat a node absent from NodeToStatusMap as UnschedulableAndUnresolvable

detection.reason: whether a custom scheduler binary is in use is not visible in the inventory; the stock kube-scheduler image name is the only hint and a custom build can reuse it

quote: For developers of out-of-tree PostFilter plugins, note that the semantics of NodeToStatusMap are changing: A node with an absent value in the NodeToStatusMap should be interpreted as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status
remediation: Only clusters running a custom-built kube-scheduler with an out-of-tree PostFilter plugin are affected. A plugin that treats a missing entry as "schedulable" now considers nodes the filters never reached; rebuild it against the 1.30 framework semantics before rolling the control plane.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[*].image}{"\n"}{end}'  # an image other than registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler is a custom build whose PostFilter plugins must follow the new semantics

title: A kubelet configured with swapBehavior LimitedSwap refuses to start on a cgroup v1 node

detection.reason: the node's cgroup version is not in Node status and the kubelet config is not a collected object; every node is a candidate

quote: Kubelet would fail if NodeSwap was used with LimitedSwap and cgroupv1 node.
remediation: From 1.30 the kubelet exits at startup with "swap feature is enabled and LimitedSwap but it is only supported with cgroupv2" (cmd/kubelet/app/server.go) when `memorySwap.swapBehavior: LimitedSwap` is set on a node whose cgroup hierarchy is v1; on 1.29 the setting was silently ignored there. Either move those nodes to cgroup v2 (systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1) or drop `swapBehavior` (the 1.30 default is `NoSwap`) before upgrading their kubelet.
verifyCommand: for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do echo "== $n"; kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$n/proxy/configz" | jq -c '.kubeletconfig | {memorySwap, featureGates}'; done  # a node showing swapBehavior LimitedSwap must be on cgroup v2 (stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup is cgroup2fs) or its 1.30 kubelet will not start

title: The AppArmor beta annotations are deprecated in favour of securityContext.appArmorProfile
quote: The beta AppArmor annotations are deprecated, and AppArmor status is no longer included in the node ready condition.
remediation: Pods still annotated `container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/<container>` keep working on 1.30 (the annotation is copied into the field), but the annotation path is on its way out — 1.34 stops mirroring fields back to it. Move manifests and admission policies to `securityContext.appArmorProfile` on the pod or container. Anything that gated on AppArmor in the Node Ready condition message no longer sees it there.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations | keys[]? | startswith("container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' | sort -u  # pods still on the deprecated annotation path

title: Containers lose swap access on 1.30 unless the kubelet sets swapBehavior explicitly

detection.reason: whether the host has swap enabled and what the kubelet config says are not in the Node object; every node is a candidate

quote: In kubelet configuration, the `.memorySwap.swapBehavior` field now accepts a new value `NoSwap`, which becomes the default if unspecified.
remediation: On a 1.29 kubelet with the NodeSwap gate at its default (on since 1.28) and no `memorySwap.swapBehavior`, containers got unlimited swap (pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime falls through to ConfigureUnlimitedSwap); on 1.30 the same configuration means `NoSwap` and the cgroup swap limit becomes 0. Nodes that run with host swap enabled will see workloads that were quietly paging start to OOM. Set `swapBehavior: LimitedSwap` (cgroup v2 only) where swap is intended; the removed `UnlimitedSwap` value is a separate config-breaker finding.
verifyCommand: for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do echo "== $n"; kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$n/proxy/configz" | jq -c '.kubeletconfig | {memorySwap, failSwapOn}'; done  # a node with failSwapOn false and no swapBehavior moves from unlimited swap to NoSwap at 1.30; check swap with free -m on the host

title: kube-apiserver refuses to start when a JWT authenticator's issuer collides with the service-account issuer

detection.reason: the authentication configuration file lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

quote: The API server now detects and fails on startup if there are conflicting issuers between JWT authenticators and service account configurations.
remediation: With `--authentication-config` (StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration is beta and on from 1.30), any `jwt[].issuer.url` equal to a `--service-account-issuer` value is now a startup error instead of an ambiguous runtime match. Two more validations land with it: an OIDC username expression that evaluates to the empty string now fails authentication instead of admitting an anonymous-named user, and `username.expression` using `claims.email` must also reference `claims.email_verified` somewhere in the authenticator. Fix the file before rolling the first 1.30 control-plane node.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?' | grep -E -- '--authentication-config|--service-account-issuer|--oidc-issuer-url'  # compare the issuer URLs in that file against the service-account issuer(s); equal means kube-apiserver will not start
coversNotes: OIDC authentication will now fail if the username asserted based on a CEL expression

title: TokenRequest audit events carry the credential id under a new annotation key

detection.reason: audit consumers are outside the cluster; nothing in inventory names them

quote: The annotation used to persist the issued credential identifier is now `authentication.kubernetes.io/issued-credential-id`.
remediation: Audit pipelines, SIEM rules or dashboards that read `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` from `serviceaccounts/<name>/token` audit events must read `authentication.kubernetes.io/issued-credential-id` instead (staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/authentication/serviceaccount/util.go at v1.30.0). The old key is still what an authenticated request's own credential is recorded under; only the TokenRequest response annotation moved.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?' | grep -E -- '--audit-(policy-file|log-path|webhook-config-file)'  # an audit pipeline is configured; check its consumers for the old credential-id key

title: Pods with hostUsers: false are rejected on nodes whose runtime cannot provide user namespaces
quote: The kubelet now rejects creating the pod if `hostUserns=false` and the CRI runtime does not support user namespaces.
remediation: On 1.29 a pod asking for a user namespace (`spec.hostUsers: false`, UserNamespacesSupport beta, off by default) was started without one when the runtime lacked support; from 1.30 the kubelet fails the pod ("RuntimeClass handler does not support user namespaces"). Confirm every node's runtime advertises userns support (containerd 2.0+ / CRI-O 1.25+ on kernel 6.3+; from 1.31 visible as Node `.status.runtimeHandlers[].features.userNamespaces`) before upgrading the kubelets that host these workloads, or drop the field.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.hostUsers == false) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " on " + .spec.nodeName'  # each of these needs a userns-capable runtime on its node after 1.30

title: procMount: Unmasked is only accepted together with spec.hostUsers: false

detection.reason: the rule is a pair condition (Unmasked AND hostUsers != false); the projection carries both fields but the evaluator reads one at a time, so the hint names the Unmasked side

quote: In the Pod API, setting the alpha `procMount` field to `Unmasked` in a container now requires setting `spec.hostUsers=false` as well.
remediation: A pod template with `securityContext.procMount: Unmasked` on any container and `hostUsers` unset or true fails validation on 1.30 (ProcMountType is alpha and off by default, so only clusters that enabled it carry the field). Add `hostUsers: false` — which itself needs UserNamespacesSupport and a userns-capable runtime — or drop `procMount`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.containers[]; .securityContext.procMount == "Unmasked")) | select(.spec.hostUsers != false) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # each of these is rejected by a 1.30 apiserver on its next write
